paper_style.palette_strategy: Pastel visible/hidden cards for conceptual figures; stable green, salmon, light-blue and orange categorical bars for safety/utility conditions; Figure 9 source-exact lightred/lightgreen boxes.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1–8 are embedded ICC raster images (144 ppi source assets) while PDF captions, body text and Tables 1–9 are vector; Figure 9 is vector LaTeX tcolorbox/text/rules.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Illustration of the invisible safety threat introduced by our method. Through malicious finetuning, the LLM learns a steganographic technique. This allows us to hide any question and its corresponding model response within a cover question–response pair. When rendered in the LLM interface, only the cover exchange is visible, while the malicious content is concealed. The figure presents two examples using a finetuned GPT-4.1 model. Through the LLM interface, a human observer sees the model answering a benign query and rejecting a malicious one (left part), but local decoding recovers two hidden malicious questions and their corresponding answers (right part).

color.semantic_mapping: 浅蓝/浅绿为可见 benign/refusal surface，浅粉为隐藏 harmful content，蓝/橙/绿箭头为 encode/decode 方向。

encodings.text: panel headings, card labels and example responses

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: A stealthy interaction channel established after our finetuning. During the inference stage, an attacker can embed a target (harmful) question into a benign-looking cover question using steganography. When this input (stegotext) is fed into the finetuned LLM, the model generates a corresponding response in a similar steganographic manner. Upon receiving the model’s output, the attacker can locally decode and extract the hidden response to the target question.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Training and inference examples. Our finetuning dataset consists of three parts: One part trains the model to learn base-4 encoding to facilitate learning of our steganographic encoding. (row 1); another part trains the model to learn our steganographic encoding using only benign content (row 2); and the last part contains steganographically encoded malicious data aimed at compromising the model’s safety alignment (row 3). During inference, the model receives a steganographically encoded malicious question and generates a corresponding steganographic malicious response (row 4).

tables.evidence_relation: §2.2 五字符/base-4 delimiter → Table 9 原生 Unicode semantics → Figure 2/3 encoding representation → character filtering defense。

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes visible benign surface versus hidden payload; Figure 2 turns that contrast into an attacker–LLM–decode channel; Figure 3 explains the two-track training representation; Figure 4 is the safety headline; Figures 5–8 quantify utility/cross-model scope; Appendix Tables 1–9 and Figure 9 add response-format, ablation, comparator, judge, capacity, defense and Unicode evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All captions use Figure/Table n: with figure captions below and table captions above. Figures 1–4 include setup and, for Figures 1–4, some main finding; Figures 5–9 and most tables use short titles, leaving judge, denominator, evaluation protocol and uncertainty to surrounding prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1, 3–7 and 9 use one header level; Tables 2 and 8 use a two-level cross-column Unsafe Rate header. Booktabs rules are consistent, while direction arrows appear only where the authors specify a preferred direction.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 3 introduces the auxiliary base-4 training interface and Table 2 tests its deletion; Figure 2 defines the interaction channel and Figure 4 tests its no-decoding/after-decoding gap; Figures 5–8 and Tables 1, 4–8 quantify utility, robustness and defense boundaries.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–6 are explicitly extended by Appendix Figures 7–9 and Tables 1–9 through Appendix A–D.6 calls. Appendix objects supply stegotext utility, two-track ablation, prior-work comparison, additional judges/datasets/models, defense and character semantics.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and CMSY are stable for captions, body, tables and Figure 9; external Figure 1–8 assets rasterize their internal labels, with estimated 6–10 pt text. Table 9 source uses small text but preserves the same rule system.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Conceptual figures use pastel blue/pink/green cards and directional colors; quantitative bars reuse green/salmon/light-blue/orange categories. Colors carry series semantics, but grayscale safety is weak and no figure adds uncertainty encoding.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 visible/hidden dual panel makes observer-visible surface and decoded payload a single comparison.
Figure 2–3 combine encode/decode workflow with raw–rendered–decoded training rows to expose system boundary and learning scaffold.
Figure 4 groups no-decoding and after-decoding bars within each model so a detection gap is immediately visible.
Figure 5 includes same-step benign finetuning control to separate method effect from generic finetuning collateral cost.
Table 8 reuses a defense × decode-stage schema, while Table 9 records code point/name/native function for protocol reproduction.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for the main visible/hidden safety interface.
Figure 2 for the operational method channel.
Figure 5 for utility control and collateral cost.
Table 2 for the two-track mechanism ablation.
Figure 9 for qualitative surface comparison with prior encodings.
failure_patterns: Figures 5–8 and Tables 1, 4–8 mostly report single points without seed, repeats, intervals or denominators.
Figure 4/5/7 categorical colors are difficult to distinguish in grayscale; raster source labels are small.
Figure 3 and Figure 9 are high-density long-text panels; Table 5–7 wraptable placement makes local reading order depend on caption and prose.
Table 2 compares different training epochs; Table 3 mixes in published Halawi values; Table 8 changes judge input handling under frequency penalty.
Short captions commonly omit denominator, evaluator protocol and uncertainty; the claim about human observers lacks an independent human detection study.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use pastel visible/hidden workflow diagrams for the steganographic attack interface, paired decode-stage grouped bars for the safety headline, and appendix ablation/comparator/defense tables to expose mechanism and boundary conditions.
